A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same MMSLT study, with matching methods, experiments, equations, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; supplementary material mentioned in the text is unavailable and is not treated as added or deleted content.

before.justification: V1 reports original MMSLT experiments on PHOENIX14T and CSL-Daily, component ablations, and qualitative translation results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results and adds an alignment-only ablation result in Table 3.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 changes the adapter description from a convolution and max-pooling layer to two successive convolution/pooling stages. The PDFs do not establish whether this represents an architectural modification or corrected implementation detail. The remaining pipeline and objectives match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate German sign-language translation on PHOENIX14T and Chinese sign-language translation on CSL-Daily. The added ablation uses the existing PHOENIX14T test set without expanding task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds an internal alignment-only comparator without GSD-MLLM or the description mapper. The external comparator sets in Tables 1 and 2, and the MLLM and description-encoder comparison sets, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The ablation design gains a control enabling alignment while disabling generated descriptions and the mapper. Existing dataset splits and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Table 2's expanded punctuation note clarifies the existing VAP evaluation treatment rather than establishing a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Table 3 expands from five to six configurations, retaining the previous conditions and adding alignment alone. This permits a direct test of whether generated descriptions provide benefits beyond alignment. The other reported ablations and translation examples are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional ablation follows the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: The new alignment-only row reports BLEU-1/2/3/4 of 47.29/36.43/28.96/23.77 and ROUGE of 46.53. Existing table scores are retained, including MMSLT test BLEU-4 of 25.73 on PHOENIX14T and 21.11 on CSL-Daily. These are added results, not improved scores for the full model.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same mappings and objectives. Changing the alignment-pair index bound from N to B makes the prose consistent with the already batch-based loss; it does not introduce new mathematical reasoning. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain first use of an off-the-shelf MLLM for this framework, multimodal alignment, efficient inference through the description mapper, and state-of-the-art gloss-free results on the same benchmarks. The broader closing outlook does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 adds an interpretation that generated descriptions benefit alignment beyond alignment alone. Section 4.1 removes specific facial-description failure examples, although the introduction retains the general limitation. The conclusion also extends its prospective outlook to multimodal learning across computer vision.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository address, specifies the adapter's successive convolution/pooling stages, and explains that the reported VAP scores exclude Chinese-punctuation conversion using Python's replace function. These improve documented access and implementation detail; repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The same 70 cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. An existing GFSLT-VLP citation is additionally attached to the encoder discussion, without introducing a new cited work or materially changing the novelty argument.

P1.justification: V2 standardizes the abbreviation SL, clarifies GSD-MLLM as preprocessing, edits wording and author footnotes, and adds an acknowledgement section. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 are redrawn, Table 1 moves from page 7 to page 6, and Table 3 gains a row and reorders retained conditions. Other changes include shorter metric headers, revised captions, and repositioning the qualitative-results table.

improvement.justification: The new alignment-only control provides more direct support for the contribution of generated descriptions: BLEU-4 is 23.77 without them versus 25.04 with them under alignment. The code pointer and punctuation clarification improve reproducibility information. Removing specific facial-error examples slightly reduces limitation detail, but the general warning remains. These are useful, limited gains rather than a substantial scientific overhaul.
